Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026
Scch-23 1 Mvc-3375/2024
Kabc020223412024
 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.

(Scch-23)
 Dated This The 6th Day Of March-2026

Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani
 B.Com. Ll.B, (Spl)
 Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm
 Member - Mact, Bengaluru.

Petitioner : Miss. Aditi. S,
 D/o Shanmugam Ramu,
 Aged about 23 years,
 R/at : No.162, Embassy Heritage  8th Main, Malleshwaram,
 Bengaluru-560055.
(By Sri.V.Venkataramappa, Adv)

v/s  Respondent : The Managing Director,
 BMTC, Shanthinagar,
 Double Road,
 Bengaluru-560027.
(By Advocate: Sri.B.P. Mahendra)
JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 22.02.2024 at about 9.30 a.m,
when the petitioner was going from home to her work in a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HU-6200, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations when she reched near Go Gas LPG Bunk, Nandigurga Main road, Bengaluru City, at that one BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-5041 which was being driven by its driver in a rash & negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner on the left side.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner fell down on the road and the left side back Tyre of the bus ran over on the right hand and right leg resulting which she sustained grievous injuries.
It is contended that immediately after the accident she was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgeries.
She has spent substantial amount towards her treatment.

It is alleged that he was working as Computer Vision Engineer and earning Rs.7,00,000/- p.a., and due to the accidental injuries she Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56893617/
1 sustained permanent disability to her and was also undergone mental shock and agony.
The respondent being the RC owner and internal insurer of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-5041 is liable to pay compensation.

3. In the written statement filed by it, the respondent transport corporation contended that the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-5041 was manning the same slowly, carefully and cautiously and with due adherence to the traffic rules and regulations.
There is no negligence on the part of the bus driver.

The accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner,
while the bus was moving near Go Gas LPG Bunk on Nandidurga Main road, the petitioner came in rash and negligent manner dashed against the footpath stone and pedal of the two wheeler of the petitioner touched center body of the bus on left side and petitioner fell down on the road along with her scooter and sustained injuries.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 22.02.2024 at about 9.30 a.m., Near Go Gas LPG Bunk, Nandidurga Main road, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-5041?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What Order or award ?
5. The petitioner got examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 10, Ex.P.12 to 16 were marked on her behalf.
Dr. Ramesha.
K.T, Professor at Department of Plastic Surgery, Victoria Hospital, was examined as PW.2.

entities.text: Department of Plastic Surgery, Victoria Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex. P.11
was marked through this witness.
In order to prove its defence, the respondent Corporation got examined the driver who was driving the BMTC bus at the time of accident as RW.1, through him got marked
Ex.R.1 document

. 
6. Arguments were addressed on both sides.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56893617/
2

7 . ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver BMTC Bus for the offences punishable under section's 279 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

8. Moreover the driver of the aforesaid BMTC bus who was examined as RW.1 and during the course of cross examination he stated that he has not seen the Sketch marked at Ex.P.5 which was produced by the applicant, the police have prepared it incorrectly.
He admitted that the charge sheet has been filed against him and further he admitted that he has not submitted application to quash the charge sheet.
He further admitted that no complaint has been filed against the applicant for overtaking his vehicle while driving a motorcycle at high speed and causing an accident.
He stated that the ground clearance of Bus is one feet and the ground clearance is of 6 inches for a two-wheeler.
He admitted that a pedal that is 6 inches high cannot collide with a guardrail that is one foot high.
Further the RW.1 also produced copy of Judgment in CC.No.1684/2024 which was marked at Ex.R.1.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, wherein he acquitted in the criminal case registered against him.
9. No doubt RW.1 was acquitted in the criminal case registered against him in CC.No.1684/2024.
But in view of the ratio laid down in the decision reported in ILR 2014 KAR 5169 acquittal in a criminal case cannot be the basis to conclude that there was no negligence on the part of the driver.

Moreover it is a settled law that the term 'rashness and negligence' has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act as compared to the word 'rashness and negligence' as finds mention in the IPC.
This is so because the chapter in Motor Vehicles Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Added more the Tribunal has to assess the factum of negligence on its own.

10. On conspectus perusal of Crime Details Form and Sketch it reflects that when petitioner was proceeding on her motorcycle on the left side of the road, at that time the driver of the BMTC bus came from same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner on the right side of petitioner vehicle and was without giving any signal or indication he suddenly took the bus to the left side of the road, due to the said impact the BMTS bus dashed to the hind side of the petitioner motorcycle.
As per the contents of charge sheet it can be easily concluded that, if the driver of the Bus was not going to the extreme left side of the road, than he would have definitely avoided the accident.
Furthermore, if the BMTC bus driver had first given way to the vehicles moving on the road on his left and then moved his bus to the left, he could have definitely avoided the accident.
As per the contents of charge sheet it can be easily concluded that, if the driver of the bus was not moving on the left side of the road, than he would have definitely avoided the accident.
Added more IMV report also discloses that the accident was not because of any mechanical defects as such this Court does not find any reason to distrust Crime Details Form and Sketch.

Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injuries.
The petitioner with the help of documentary proof had clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of Bus.
Viewed from any angle this Court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
When such is the case absolutely there is no impediment in considering the version of the petitioner herein.

The petitioner has successfully Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56893617/
3 demonstrated there is a negligence on the part of the BMTC bus driver.
With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

ISSUE NO.2 :
11.
AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited her Aadhar card at Ex.P9,
wherein her date of birth is reflected as 15.08.2000.
This indicates that she was aged (23 years 6 months 7 days) 24 years on the date of accident.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

12. As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1) Near circumferential degloving crush injury to right thigh extending from knee to pelvis 2) Near circumferential degloving crush injury to right upper limb extending from proximal arm to distal forearm.
It is needless to say that the injruies are grievous in nature.
The discharge summary Ex
.P.6 indicates that the petitioner was taken treatment as an inpatient from 22.02.2024 to 24.02.2024 and from 24.02.2024 to 11.03.2024 for a period of 18 days.

During the course of treatment she undergone surgeries in the form of :
Major debridement of the right thigh and right upper limb under GA on 22.02.2024 2) Relook debridement of right high and right upper limb under GA on 26.02.2024 3)
SSG of right thigh and right upper limb under GA on 01.03.2024.
13.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Ramesha. K.T,
Professor at Department of Plastic Surgery, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56893617/
4

entities.text: Department of Plastic Surgery, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: physical disability of 15% to the right upper limb, 15% to the right lower limb.
During the course of cross examination PW.2 admitted that he was not treated the petitioner and he has not seen the case sheet.
Further he admitted that he has seen the discharge summary.
He admitted that no fractures to the petitioner.
Further he has not assessed functional disability and was assessed physical limb for concerned limb.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the physical disability.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
When such is the case she has not sustained any fracture injury, but she sustained de-gloving injuries.
Further with a injuries sustained by the petitioner she cannot do her work effectively, as such her efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect her income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 20%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.
14.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES : The period of hospitalization of 18 days is proved with a help of discharge summaries.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.21,600/- (1,200 X 18) is awarded under this head.
15. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.

The documents discloses that petitioner had sustained Near circumferential degloving crush injury to right thigh extending from knee to pelvis 2) Near circumferential degloving crush injury to right upper limb extending from proximal arm to distal forearm.
Having regard to the injuries suffered by the petitioner and such other attending circumstances.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

16. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast 8 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.1,32,000/- (16,500 X 8) under this head.
17. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P8, the petitioner has spent Rs.7,24,753/-
towards medical expenses.
During the course of her cross examination she denied that all the medical bills amount was reimbursed from her health insurance.
But she has not produced any iota of documents in this regard.
As per Ex.P8 Sl.No.3 and 5 wherein it is mentioned the name of insurance company.
It appears that the said bills paid by health insurance company.

Hence this Aditi S vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56893617/
5
Court does not considered the bill amount of Rs.3,06,034/- and Rs.4,00,809/-.
Hence after deduction of Rs.7,06,843/-, she is entitled only Rs.17,910/- towards medical expenses.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.7,12,800/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 18 X 20/100) which is rounded off to Rs.7,12,800/- is awarded under this head.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of her life.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded under this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
21.FUTURE AND MATRIMONIAL PROSPECTS:
Some way or the other the disability of the petitioner would affect her future prospects both professionally and personally.
Obviously the matrimonial prospects of the victim/petitioner who suffered accidental injuries would be affected.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard, ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- under this head.

22. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 21,600-00 food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 1,00,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 1,32,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 17,910-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 7,12,800-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 1,50,000-00 happiness 7

Future medical expenses : -
Nil - 8
Future & matrimonial prospects.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The Respondent being the RC owner & internal insurer of the BMTC bus is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount.

With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

6 ORDER

sentences.text:
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,34,310/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/ RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
